text: I had a tooth extracted around 1 PM today. The dentist gave me a local anesthetic, and then it took quite a while. She couldn't pull the tooth out, so she used a tool to drill a hole, creating a grip on the tooth to make it easier to extract. This was my first time having a tooth extracted, and it was terrifying! The needle used for drilling came loose, landed on my tongue, and was about to go down my throat. I quickly raised my hand to rinse my mouth because I initially thought the tooth had just come loose. But it was the needle! I was so shocked. When I rinsed my mouth, I saw the needle and wondered what would happen if it had gotten stuck in my throat. I told the dentist, "Doctor, why is there a needle? It's going to get stuck in my throat!" The dentist said, "It won't get stuck, I was just about to see." I was so confused. She didn't apologize and wouldn't let me rinse my mouth. I had to reluctantly let her continue, still terrified and apprehensive. I quickly paid and left because I was so scared. This was a female dentist. I wish dentists would be more careful and considerate of their patients.
